title: bash command history
whyItMatters: On older macOS versions and in many terminals, bash records typed commands. Those commands can expose paths, servers and entered secrets.
source: GNU Bash manual, HISTFILE: defaults to ~/.bash_history; listed in the macforensics.app artifact cheat sheet (Shell History)
notes: Only metadata is recorded; command lines are never opened. bash_sessions and other variants are not covered by this rule.

steps: Quit Terminal and any other terminal app so the history file is not written again.
Open the file named in the plan in a text editor and copy out any command you need to keep.
Delete the file, then empty the Trash, so the next shell starts with empty history.
cleanup.risk: Every command you typed is lost, including passwords or tokens typed by mistake and still readable in it.
